stem: In a circle, minor arc \(AB\) has a length of \(5\pi\), and the circumference of the circle is \(18\pi\). Point \(C\) lies on the circle on major arc \(AB\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(ACB\)?
solution: Minor arc \(AB\) is \(\frac{5\pi}{18\pi} = \frac{5}{18}\) of the circle, so its central angle is \(\frac{5}{18}(360) = 100^{\circ}\).
Angle \(ACB\) is an inscribed angle intercepting that arc, so it is half the central angle: \(50^{\circ}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(25\) halves the inscribed angle a second time; only the central angle is halved once.
explanation.B: Correct. The arc measures \(\frac{5}{18}(360) = 100^{\circ}\), and the inscribed angle is half of that: \(50^{\circ}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(100\) is the measure of the arc (the central angle), not the inscribed angle \(ACB\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(200\) doubles the central angle instead of halving it.

verify:
frac=Rational(5,18)
central=frac*360
ans=central/2
assert central==100 and ans==50
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
assert value(choices['C'])==central and value(choices['D'])==2*central
